newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 31.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Seven of the 13 regional wage boards all over the country have granted wage increases or cost-of-living allowances to workers. (BULLETIN)

- President Ramos yesterday reiterated his confidence in the Philippine National Police, saying that the country's economic gains were partly due to its efforts to preserve law and order. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- Congress increased the budget of the Department of Public Works and Highways by 10.9 billion pesos for 1997, enabling legislators to claim credit for the financing of more infrastructure projects a year before the 1998 elections. (JOURNAL/TIMES)
- The stock market celebrated news of a 6.8 percent gross national product growth with the blue-chip index of the Philippine Stock Exchange surging to a historical high of 3,392.75. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- Reclaimed property developers at the Manila Bay have closed ranks to reiterate their commitment to pursue the Boulevard 2000 project despite a brewing controversy on one of its key participants - Amari Coastal Bay Development Corp. (INQUIRER/JOURNAL/STAR)
- Petron Corp, the country's most profitable oil refiner, posted an improved net income of 4.238 billion pesos in 1996, up 5.4 percent from 4.02 billion pesos the previous year. (STAR/TIMES)
